title: cli-contract section 2.1 kind table omits 13 of 38 manifest kinds, and the LCLI-528 guard only checks one direction
description:
Found by the independent review (opum-workflow:review-assignment, run wf_141a23b7-191) of LCLI-528 (PR opum-ai/lore-cli#491). Two related doc/contract gaps, both PRE-EXISTING and deliberately NOT fixed there.

(1) docs/reference/cli-contract.md section 2.1 says the kind table mirrors the capability manifest, but it is not exhaustive: of the 38 kinds buildManifest() declares, 13 are absent from the table -- backlog.adoption.apply, backlog.adoption.preview, backlog.adoption.rollback, backlog.adoption.status, changed.result, explorer.artifact, impact.result, path.result, projection.export, provenance.result, read.concept, snapshot.result, version.

(2) test/lcli528-kind-registry-matches-manifest.test.ts (added by LCLI-528) asserts only ONE direction -- every kind the table attributes to a command is manifest-declared. It stays green when rows are DELETED, so it cannot catch further omitting drift. A mutation proof recorded by the review: deleting 3 rows keeps it green (kinds 25 -> 22).

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deliberately left undecided here (a contract-design call for opum-doc, routed by opum-agent): must section 2.1 be exhaustive (add the 13 missing rows), and correspondingly should the guard check BOTH directions (table set == manifest command-kind set)? The answer decides whether (1) is a doc bug to fix or an intended summary, and whether (2) is strengthened.

Also folded in from the same review: docs/reference/cli-contract.md line 221 prose says the version/help meta envelopes are not in the manifest, which is inaccurate for version -- the manifest DOES declare it via globalFlags[].kind (src/core/manifest.ts:231); only bare help is genuinely undeclared. The guard decision to skip that row is correct; only the stated reason is imprecise.

NOT STARTED. Priority low. Do not begin until the design question is answered.
plan: 1. Add the missing §2.1 rows for the kinds the manifest declares but the table omits, each data-shape summary derived from the command itself.
2. Add kind: help to the help global flag (src/core/manifest.ts) so the meta row matches the manifest.
3. Change the LCLI-528 guard to SET EQUALITY (table kind set == manifest declared set), both directions.
4. Correct the §2.1 prose: version IS declared (globalFlags[].kind), and after the help kind so is help.
5. Gates: full bun test, lore check, lint, typecheck. Review, record, land.
implementationNotes: PARKED at low priority per the operator (relayed by opum-doc), 2026-10-05T22:07Z: do NOT start. The fleet is pausing hardening work for a new campaign. Ruling on the open design question recorded above, DEC-160 amended again (opum-doc): option A -- the one additive kind: "help" on the help global flag IS allowed, matching the version flag (src/core/manifest.ts:231) and the manifest docstring requirement that a consumer read commands[].kind, commands[].resultKinds AND globalFlags[].kind -- so the guard can be exactly the set equality DEC-160 amended describes. When this is taken up: add the 13 missing section 2.1 rows, add kind: "help" to the help global flag (src/core/manifest.ts:232), change the guard to set equality, and correct the line-221 prose.

Completed on branch fix/LCLI-677-cli-contract-kind-registry, per DEC-160 amended (opum-doc), option A -- already recorded in this task note. WHAT CHANGED: (1) docs/reference/cli-contract.md §2.1 gains the 12 kinds the manifest declared but the table omitted (the four backlog.adoption.*, path.result, impact.result, snapshot.result, changed.result, provenance.result, explorer.artifact, projection.export, read.concept), each shaped from its CLI-surface section; §2.1 is now declared EXHAUSTIVE. (2) The guard test now asserts SET EQUALITY, not one direction -- it stayed green when rows were DELETED, the omission drift it existed to catch; it now names the drift per direction and checks for duplicate rows. (3) src/core/manifest.ts: the --help global flag carries kind "help" (like --version), so both meta envelopes are manifest-declared and §2.1 meta row is counted, not skipped. (4) The line-221 prose is corrected: version/help ARE in the manifest via globalFlags[].kind. RECONCILIATION vs the design note wording: the note says 13 rows; under set equality it is 12, because version is already carried by the §2.1 meta row -- the 13th was only "missing" while the guard skipped that row. COUPLING (reported): adding rows grew cli-contract.md, a declared source of the verification profile, which sat at 99.4 percent of its budget; its max_tokens moved 96000 -> 96400 per that profile own note that the number moves with edits to a declared source. lore check is back to its ONE pre-existing warning (implementation, the ADR-0025 residual, untouched). EVIDENCE: the guard reds on a deleted row (names graph.export) and on a removed help kind (names help); a delta probe shows 39 == 39, empty both ways. GATES: full suite 4982 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; lint, typecheck, lore check clean.
finalSummary: cli-contract §2.1 is now an EXHAUSTIVE kind registry equal to the capability manifest, and the LCLI-528 guard asserts that equality rather than one direction. Twelve manifest-declared kinds were missing from the table (the four backlog.adoption.* operations, path.result, impact.result, snapshot.result, changed.result, provenance.result, explorer.artifact, projection.export and read.concept); the --help global flag now carries kind help so both meta envelopes are manifest-declared; and the line-221 prose is corrected. The old guard stayed green when rows were DELETED, so it could not catch the omission it existed to catch; it now reds in BOTH directions, proven by mutation. Adding rows grew a declared source of the verification profile, so that profile budget moved 96000 -> 96400 -- what its own note says the number does, moving with edits to a declared source. Verified by the two guard mutation proofs, a manifest-to-table delta probe (39 == 39, no difference either way), and the full suite 4982 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail with lore check exit 0.
